02-261.name: Quantitative Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory
02-261.rationale: Biological laboratory experimentation and quantitative cell/molecular research are the central subject.

02-262.name: Computation and Biology Integrated Research Lab
02-262.rationale: The integrated laboratory centers experimental and computational biological research.

15-112.name: Fundamentals of Programming and Computer Science
15-112.rationale: The description teaches Python programming, program design, testing and debugging.

15-122.name: Principles of Imperative Computation
15-122.rationale: Imperative programming, correct implementations and basic algorithms/data structures are central.

15-150.name: Principles of Functional Programming
15-150.rationale: Functional programming, types, recursion and program construction are central.

15-151.name: Mathematical Foundations for Computer Science
15-151.rationale: Logic, sets, induction, combinatorics and mathematical proof are the explicit focus.

15-210.name: Parallel and Sequential Data Structures and Algorithms
15-210.rationale: Design, analysis and implementation of parallel/sequential algorithms and data structures are central.

15-213.name: Introduction to Computer Systems
15-213.rationale: Program execution, storage, communication and systems-level performance are central.

15-251.name: Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science
15-251.rationale: Theoretical computer-science problem solving covers algorithms, complexity, automata and computation.

15-259.name: Probability and Computing
15-259.rationale: The course introduces probability theory motivated by computing applications.

15-386.name: Neural Computation
15-386.rationale: Computational neuroscience seeks to explain biological neurons and natural intelligence, rather than primarily train AI models.

15-387.name: Computational Perception
15-387.rationale: Computational models investigate biological/psychological natural perception; cognitive mechanisms are the central domain.

15-463.name: Computational Photography
15-463.rationale: Optical imaging, graphics, vision and computational photography combine physical-domain and vision methods without a single clear primary category.

15-482.name: Autonomous Agents
15-482.rationale: Integrated autonomous agents use AI reasoning, perception, planning and learning.

15-494.name: Cognitive Robotics: The Future of Robot Toys
15-494.rationale: Robot cognition projects implement perception, recognition, planning and autonomous manipulation.

05-317.name: Design of Artificial Intelligence Products
05-317.rationale: User-centered AI product/service design combines design practice and human interaction; AI use does not establish a primary AI-methods subject.

05-318.name: Human AI Interaction
05-318.rationale: Human agency, ethics and interaction are taught alongside weekly construction of AI systems; neither focus is safely discarded.

05-391.name: Designing Human Centered Software
05-391.rationale: Human-centered interface design, prototyping and user evaluation span software construction and human interaction.

11-411.name: Natural Language Processing
11-411.rationale: Language representations, learning, neural models and NLP applications establish AI-method content.

11-423.name: ConLanging: Lrng Ling & Lang Tech via Constru Artif. Lang
11-423.rationale: Constructed-language work centers linguistic variation, language/culture and language policy; technologies support that exploration.

11-441.name: Machine Learning with Graphs
11-441.rationale: Graph neural learning, models and reasoning are explicit methods.

11-442.name: Search Engines
11-442.rationale: Information retrieval models and distributed search architecture combine AI-related retrieval and systems construction.

11-485.name: Introduction to Deep Learning
11-485.rationale: Neural-network theory, architectures, training and implementation establish deep-learning methods.

11-492.name: Speech Technology for Conversational AI
11-492.rationale: Speech recognition, generation and language models support conversational-AI implementation.

10-403.name: Deep Reinforcement Learning & Control
10-403.rationale: Learning autonomous-agent behavior through reinforcement and imitation is central.

10-405.name: Machine Learning with Large Datasets (Undergraduate)
10-405.rationale: Scalable learning methods and parallel/memory/computation infrastructure share the course focus.

10-414.name: Deep Learning Systems: Algorithms and Implementation
10-414.rationale: Building an efficient deep-learning library combines device-level systems, differentiation and AI model design.

10-417.name: Intermediate Deep Learning
10-417.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised deep representations and neural architectures are central.

10-418.name: Machine Learning for Structured Data
10-418.rationale: Structured prediction studies graphical/neural models, inference and learning.

10-422.name: Foundations of Learning, Game Theory, and Their Connections
10-422.rationale: Connections between machine-learning theory and algorithmic game theory give both AI and mathematical foundations substantial scope.

10-423.name: Generative AI
10-423.rationale: Generative/foundation models, training and adaptation establish explicit AI methods.

10-424.name: Bayesian Methods in Machine Learning
10-424.rationale: Bayesian inference is taught through ML estimation, classification, Gaussian processes and adaptive learning.

10-425.name: Introduction to Convex Optimization
10-425.rationale: Convex optimization properties, duality and numerical methods are central; machine learning motivates the mathematics.

16-161.name: Artificial Intelligence and Humanity
16-161.rationale: Historical, social and ethical interpretations of humanity and intelligent technology are central.

16-280.name: Intelligent Robot Systems
16-280.rationale: Robotic cognition uses search, planning, perception and neural networks; software infrastructure supports these methods.

16-350.name: Planning Techniques for Robotics
16-350.rationale: Autonomous robot planning theory and implementations are central.

16-362.name: Mobile Robot Algorithms Laboratory
16-362.rationale: Robotic autonomy uses sensing, planning and exploration algorithms in progressively developed simulations.

16-384.name: Robot Kinematics and Dynamics
16-384.rationale: Robot mechanics covers transformations, kinematics, Jacobians and equations of motion; robotics association alone does not make it AI.

16-385.name: Computer Vision
16-385.rationale: Detection, recognition and computational vision/perception are explicit methods.

16-397.name: Art, Conflict and Technology
16-397.rationale: Artistic practice, political conflict, identity and technological power are interpreted historically and culturally.

16-467.name: Introduction to Human Robot Interaction
16-467.rationale: The course centers human-robot interaction, psychology and design/evaluation of interaction studies; programming is not necessary.

16-735.name: Ethics and Robotics
16-735.rationale: Robotics/AI are examined through ethics, culture and societal power.

07-128.name: First Year Seminar
07-128.rationale: Orientation and rotating historical/research talks do not establish one stable primary subject.

07-135.name: Grand Challenge First-Year Seminar: Designing Better Human-AI Futures
07-135.rationale: Societal bias, fairness and policy in human-AI systems are the guiding problem.

07-280.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning I
07-280.rationale: Search, learning, reinforcement and implementation of landmark AI systems are explicit methods.

07-380.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning II
07-380.rationale: The second AI/ML course extends foundational methods with current AI research topics.

07-402.name: SCS Leadership Development Seminar
07-402.rationale: Leadership and organizational/personal development are the named practice; SCS affiliation does not imply computing foundations.

17-200.name: Ethics and Policy Issues in Computing
17-200.rationale: Ethical and policy analysis of computing decisions is central.

17-333.name: Privacy Policy, Law, and Technology
17-333.rationale: Privacy law, policy and philosophical analysis guide the course; technologies are examined in that context.

17-416.name: Responsible AI & AI Governance: Identifying and Mitigating Risks
17-416.rationale: Technical alignment/privacy/model-risk methods and policy/organizational AI governance are combined without one clearly dominant subject.

17-562.name: Computer and AI Law
17-562.rationale: Legal process, intellectual property, regulation and law of technology are central.
